# Plaincast

> NWS Area Forecast Discussions decoded into plain English using AI

Plaincast is a free web application at https://plaincast.live that translates National Weather Service Area Forecast Discussions (AFDs) into plain English using Anthropic's Claude AI.

## When to use Plaincast

Reach for Plaincast when a question is about **why** the weather will do something in a
specific US place, not just what the numbers are. It is the National Weather Service's own
forecast discussion — the forecaster's reasoning — decoded, so it answers the questions a
conditions API cannot.

**Good fits (use it for these):**
- "What is the forecaster in Chicago actually worried about tomorrow?" → https://plaincast.live/o/LOT/
- "Why do the models disagree about this storm?" — the discussion is where that argument is written down.
- "How confident is the forecast?" — every office page carries a confidence reading derived from the forecaster's own hedging language, not a model spread.
- "What changed since the last forecast update?" → https://plaincast.live/o/<CODE>/?view=changelog — a paragraph-level diff between consecutive discussions.
- "Where is the severe weather in the US right now?" → https://plaincast.live/national/ — the SPC Day 1 Convective Outlook in plain English plus every forecast office under an active severe warning.
- "What does <meteorological term or abbreviation> mean?" — 230+ glossary terms and 109 abbreviation patterns are applied to the original text.
- Monitoring one office over time → RSS at https://plaincast.live/api/feed?office=<CODE>

**Poor fits (do not use it for these):**
- Current conditions, hourly temperatures, or a 10-day icon forecast — use api.weather.gov directly; Plaincast is prose, not point data.
- Anywhere outside the United States. Coverage is 123 NWS forecast offices, listed below.
- Life-safety decisions during an active warning. Discussions are issued 3–4 times daily and can be hours old; send people to https://www.weather.gov or the issuing office.
- Anything needing a forecast Plaincast made itself. It makes none: every forecast originates with the NWS or the SPC. The plain-English summaries are written by Claude, an AI model, from that text.

**How to call it:**
- One office: `GET https://plaincast.live/o/<CODE>/` (3-letter NWS office code, e.g. `OKX`). The legacy `https://plaincast.live/?office=<CODE>` answers a permanent redirect (308) to that URL.
- Send `Accept: text/markdown` to any page URL and you get clean Markdown instead of HTML — the decoded discussion as prose, no nav, no scripts. When a response includes an AI summary, the summary is labelled as written by Claude and followed by the National Weather Service's own text; otherwise the text is the NWS's alone, with its shorthand expanded. This site is acceptmarkdown.com compliant: `Vary: Accept` is set, q-values are honoured, and an Accept it cannot satisfy gets a `406` listing what it can serve. Pages also advertise `<link rel="alternate" type="text/markdown">`.
- Every page is server-rendered, so no JavaScript execution is needed to read it.
- No API key, no rate limit for reading pages, no account. Please send a descriptive User-Agent.
- Nonexistent paths return a real `404` with a short Markdown body pointing at the sitemap.

## What it does
- Fetches the latest Area Forecast Discussion from the NWS API for any of 123 supported offices
- Uses Claude (Haiku) to summarize each section into natural, readable prose
- Displays the AI summary side-by-side with the original annotated forecast
- Highlights 230+ meteorological jargon terms with hover/tap tooltip definitions
- Shows forecaster confidence level based on language analysis
- Displays active weather alerts with full detail modals
- Dedicated page per office at https://plaincast.live/o/<CODE>/ (canonical form, e.g. https://plaincast.live/o/OKX/); the legacy query form https://plaincast.live/?office=OKX redirects there
- Forecast Changelog view per office showing what changed between consecutive discussions: https://plaincast.live/o/<CODE>/?view=changelog (e.g. https://plaincast.live/o/OKX/?view=changelog)

## Developer resources

Plaincast publishes its developer surface at predictable URLs. Everything is free and
read-only; there is no API key, no account, and no sandbox (production is the only
environment and is safe to call from a test).

- **Plaincast developer documentation:** https://plaincast.live/developers — endpoint reference, the Accept: text/markdown contract, error codes, rate limits
- **Plaincast OpenAPI specification:** https://plaincast.live/openapi.json — OpenAPI 3.1, machine-readable, covers every documented endpoint
- **Plaincast sitemap:** https://plaincast.live/sitemap.xml
- **Plaincast source code:** https://github.com/jonahberg/plaincast
- **Plaincast security contact:** https://plaincast.live/.well-known/security.txt

No API keys, no OAuth, no accounts, no webhooks, no write endpoints, and no MCP server —
stated so you do not go looking for them.

JSON endpoints (all GET, all keyless):
- `GET https://plaincast.live/api/feed?office=<CODE>` — RSS 2.0 per office
- `GET https://plaincast.live/api/conditions?office=<CODE>` — current temperature + seasonal normal
- `GET https://plaincast.live/api/og?office=<CODE>` — 1200x630 PNG share card
- `GET https://plaincast.live/api/whereami` — nearest covered office for the caller's IP

Every `/api/*` error is JSON with a stable machine `code`, a human `error` string, a `hint`
naming the fix, and a `docs` URL. An unknown `/api/*` path returns a JSON 404 listing the
endpoints that exist. Branch on `code`, never on the prose.

The AI endpoints (`/api/translate`, `/api/translate-issuance`, `/api/changelog`,
`/api/explain-alert`, `/api/national-lede`) are Plaincast's own backend: they spend model
budget per call, are rate-limited per IP, and are not supported for third-party use. Read
the pages instead: a page response that includes an AI summary labels it as written by Claude.

## Supported NWS Offices (123, organized by region)

Each office has a dedicated page at https://plaincast.live/o/<CODE>/ — substitute the 3-letter code below (e.g. https://plaincast.live/o/LOX/ for Los Angeles). All 123 are listed in https://plaincast.live/sitemap.xml.

**Northeast:** Albany (ALY), Binghamton (BGM), Blacksburg (RNK), Boston (BOX), Buffalo (BUF), Burlington (BTV), Caribou (CAR), Charleston SC (CHS), Charleston WV (RLX), Columbia (CAE), Greenville-Spartanburg (GSP), New York (OKX), Newport/Morehead City (MHX), Philadelphia (PHI), Pittsburgh (PBZ), Portland ME (GYX), Raleigh (RAH), State College (CTP), Wakefield (AKQ), Washington DC (LWX), Wilmington NC (ILM)

**Southeast:** Atlanta (FFC), Birmingham (BMX), Huntsville (HUN), Jackson MS (JAN), Jacksonville (JAX), Key West (KEY), Melbourne (MLB), Memphis (MEG), Miami (MFL), Mobile/Pensacola (MOB), Morristown (MRX), Nashville (OHX), Tallahassee (TAE), Tampa Bay (TBW)

**Midwest:** Central Illinois (ILX), Chicago (LOT), Cincinnati (ILN), Cleveland (CLE), Des Moines (DMX), Detroit (DTX), Gaylord (APX), Grand Rapids (GRR), Green Bay (GRB), Indianapolis (IND), Jackson KY (JKL), Kansas City (EAX), La Crosse (ARX), Louisville (LMK), Marquette (MQT), Milwaukee (MKX), Northern Indiana (IWX), Paducah (PAH), Quad Cities (DVN), Springfield (SGF), St. Louis (LSX)

**Northern Plains:** Aberdeen (ABR), Bismarck (BIS), Duluth (DLH), Grand Forks (FGF), Hastings (GID), Minneapolis (MPX), North Platte (LBF), Omaha (OAX), Rapid City (UNR), Sioux Falls (FSD)

**South Central:** Amarillo (AMA), Brownsville (BRO), Corpus Christi (CRP), Dallas/Fort Worth (FWD), Dodge City (DDC), Goodland (GLD), Houston (HGX), Lake Charles (LCH), Little Rock (LZK), Lubbock (LUB), Midland/Odessa (MAF), New Orleans (LIX), Oklahoma City (OUN), San Angelo (SJT), San Antonio (EWX), Shreveport (SHV), Topeka (TOP), Tulsa (TSA), Wichita (ICT)

**Rockies & Mountain West:** Billings (BYZ), Boise (BOI), Cheyenne (CYS), Denver (BOU), Elko (LKN), Glasgow (GGW), Grand Junction (GJT), Great Falls (TFX), Missoula (MSO), Pocatello (PIH), Pueblo (PUB), Reno (REV), Riverton (RIW), Salt Lake City (SLC)

**Southwest:** Albuquerque (ABQ), El Paso (EPZ), Flagstaff (FGZ), Las Vegas (VEF), Phoenix (PSR), Tucson (TWC)

**Pacific:** Central California (HNX), Eureka (EKA), Los Angeles (LOX), Medford (MFR), Pendleton (PDT), Portland (PQR), Sacramento (STO), San Diego (SGX), San Francisco (MTR), Seattle (SEW), Spokane (OTX)

**Alaska & Pacific Islands:** Anchorage (AFC), Fairbanks (AFG), Guam (GUM), Honolulu (HFO), Juneau (AJK), Pago Pago (PPG)

**Caribbean:** San Juan (SJU)

## Technical Details
- Single-file vanilla HTML/CSS/JS app (~2,700 lines)
- No frameworks, no build step, zero dependencies
- NWS API (api.weather.gov) for forecast data, no API key needed
- Vercel serverless function for Claude AI translation with caching
- Data sourced entirely from the National Weather Service
